title: L&T Wins Ultra-Mega Offshore Order Worth Over ₹15,000 Crore From ADNOC
excerpt: Larsen & Toubro's hydrocarbon offshore unit secures another blockbuster Middle East contract, reinforcing India's engineering giant as a dominant force in global energy infrastructure.
body:
• L&T Energy Hydrocarbon Offshore has secured an ultra-mega order from ADNOC Offshore valued at over ₹15,000 crore ($1.8 billion), covering multiple offshore EPCIC packages in the Middle East.
  • The contract includes engineering, procurement, construction, installation, and commissioning of offshore structures along with upgrades to existing facilities.
  • This is L&T's latest in a string of ultra-mega wins in the Gulf region, following a record ₹15,000 crore QatarEnergy LNG contract in March 2025 and additional orders from unnamed Middle East clients.
  • L&T's hydrocarbon offshore unit is chasing an estimated $57 billion in energy contracts globally in 2026, nearly matching the entire offshore EPCI market.

Another Mega Win in the Gulf

Larsen & Toubro has added another ultra-mega contract to its rapidly expanding Middle East portfolio, with its hydrocarbon offshore business securing a major order from ADNOC Offshore valued at over ₹15,000 crore. The contract, announced on Monday, covers multiple offshore packages including the engineering, procurement, construction, and installation of offshore structures, along with upgrades to existing facilities.

The win cements L&T's position as one of the most prolific Indian contractors operating in the Gulf's energy sector. Under L&T's internal classification, orders exceeding ₹15,000 crore qualify as "ultra-mega" — and the company has been accumulating them at a remarkable pace.

A Pattern of Dominance

The ADNOC contract follows a series of landmark wins for L&T across the region. In March 2025, the company secured what it called the largest single order in its history — an ultra-mega offshore contract from QatarEnergy LNG for the North Field Production Sustainability Offshore Compression Project, also valued at over ₹15,000 crore.

Since then, L&T has secured additional ultra-mega orders from unnamed Middle East clients, including a consortium arrangement with Greek contractor Consolidated Contractors Group for a natural gas liquids plant. The company's offshore unit has built a track record over three decades, executing projects involving fixed platforms, subsea pipelines, brownfield modifications, and decommissioning across both shallow and deep-water fields.

"The ultra-mega order reaffirms L&T's position as a trusted partner in delivering mega energy infrastructure."

— S.N. Subrahmanyan, Chairman and Managing Director, L&T

Scale of Ambition

Industry analysts note that L&T's energy ambitions are now approaching a scale that rivals the entire global offshore EPCI market. According to a LinkedIn analysis by energy consultant Pablo Costa, L&T is actively pursuing approximately $57 billion in energy contracts in 2026 — against a total global offshore EPCI market forecast of $59 billion for the year.

The company's international orders accounted for more than half of its order inflows for the quarter ending December 2024, and 42 per cent of its total outstanding order book. L&T reported consolidated profit after tax of ₹5,497 crore in Q4 FY25, a 25 per cent year-on-year increase, with quarterly revenue of ₹74,392 crore.

What It Means for India's Engineering Sector

L&T's growing dominance in Gulf energy contracts reflects a broader shift in the global EPC landscape. Indian engineering firms are increasingly winning contracts that Western majors once considered exclusively theirs, driven by competitive pricing, strong execution capabilities, and deep relationships with Gulf state energy companies.

For Indian investors and the diaspora with exposure to Indian markets, L&T's order pipeline is a bellwether for India's industrial competitiveness. The ADNOC win is also significant for the large Indian workforce in the UAE, where L&T maintains substantial fabrication and operational infrastructure.

ADNOC, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, has been accelerating its offshore development programme as part of the UAE's strategy to expand oil and gas production capacity even as it invests in energy transition technologies.
